texts: Coffee beans are actually the seeds of a fruit — the coffee cherry — and if you plant one, you'll grow a completely different variety due to how coffee genetics work through cross-pollination.

Finland consumes more coffee per capita than any other country, averaging about 12 kilograms per person annually, partly because of the Finnish concept of "kahvitauko" — a mandatory coffee break written into labor law.

The world's coffee supply faces a genetic bottleneck — over 60% of global coffee production comes from just one hybrid plant variety, making the entire industry dangerously vulnerable to disease and climate change.
